blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — While they are not expecting fuel price spikes similar to what happened last March 2026, when the war between the United States (US) and Iran started, the Department of Energy (DOE) does not expect fuel costs to go down to pre-war levels even by the end of the year. In an ambush interview at the Batasang Pambansa on Monday, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin was asked about the looming fuel price hikes which will see gasoline costs rising by over P4 per liter, diesel by over P8 per liter, and kerosene by at least P6 per liter.
